idle:
Use case: identity-preserve pixel sprite animation.
Input image 1 is the APPROVED CHARACTER to animate. Preserve THIS EXACT character's slim body proportions, pink hair shape, blue eye, head-to-body ratio, bubble helmet, white suit, pink trim at elbows/knees/ankles, grey joint cuffs, cyan tiny accent, pixel size/detail and right-facing near-side three-quarter angle. Do not replace her with another face, front-facing character, squat chibi or enlarged head. Hair all inside helmet. Keep her elegant silhouette and longer slim legs. The input pose is a floating/run pose; change ONLY pose to calm standing breathing, and replace its rear jetpack unit with a SMALL plain oxygen cylinder about half that unit's volume, no jets.
Create EXACTLY FOUR coherent frames of an IDLE BREATHING ANIMATION in a SINGLE horizontal strip, in FOUR equally sized rectangular cells. Transparent background, no labels, no border, no floor, no shadows. Frame order left to right. All images upright, same scale and consistent pixel grid, each character centered identically. Use enough canvas height to fully show helmet and both feet. Maintain the source pixel-art fidelity, crisp square pixels, dark outlines, flat stepped shading, absolutely no blur, antialias or smooth gradients.
Every pose must show: stable two feet planted on same baseline, torso nearly upright with a very subtle forward lean, arms relaxed down beside body, right-facing head with SAME blue visible eye and face silhouette as reference. Do not turn the head toward camera.
Frame 1: neutral standing relaxed arms, stable legs.
Frame 2: inhale: rigid helmet+head+shoulders shift UP by one SOURCE pixel, chest extends 1 pixel, hips/legs/feet completely IDENTICAL to frame 1.
Frame 3: inhalation peak at same height, hands shift outward ONE source pixel only, one glass highlight shifts ONE pixel. Helmet, face, torso otherwise exactly same as frame 2.
Frame 4: exhale back to exact frame 1 height and pose; only pink hair tip inside helmet settles down ONE pixel.
This is a quiet subtle BREATHING loop, no walking foot motion, no sway, no big changes. The entire lower body must be copied pixel-identically from frame 1 to all four frames. Helmet and face should be the SAME drawing translated by one pixel, not independently redesigned. Use consistent shapes and palette between frames. Do not blink this time.
Transparent pixels around every sprite. Small oxygen cylinder, no jetpack, no thrusters, no weapons, no aura, no long external hair.
float:
Use case: identity-preserve pixel sprite animation.
Image 1 is the APPROVED floating character design; image 2 is her matching standing idle sheet for consistent suit and face. Animate THIS EXACT SAME GIRL, not another design. Keep source detailed pixel-art precision, slim longer limbs, original head/body ratio, pink bob / flat M fringe, BLUE eye, right-facing near-side three-quarter angle with the same one visible eye, white fitted spacesuit with pink trim and grey cuffs, small cyan accents. Hair entirely within the transparent bubble helmet. Do not make a front-facing or squat big-head chibi. Replace the rear jetpack with a SMALL plain oxygen tank like the second image, no nozzle or jets.
Make EXACTLY SIX FLOATING ANIMATION FRAMES, arranged in a 3 COLUMNS by 2 ROWS sprite sheet on a genuine transparent background. Read order top-left to top-right then bottom-left to bottom-right. All SIX cells identical size and all characters identical scale, same framing and stable horizontal torso position. No words, numbers, frame borders, floor or shadows. Crisp uniform square pixels, dark outline, simple stepped shading, NO gradients, texture, antialias or blur.
BASE POSE: very close to image 1: body tilts slightly forward, right-facing head alert, arms held away from body as if finding balance, hand open, knees gently bent, legs parted with one foot 1-2 source pixels higher. Visible near arm is extended back/down at roughly 45 degrees and far arm extends slightly forward. Neither arm must overlap the face. Float in place, no propulsion. Pink hair TIPS rise INSIDE the helmet, never outside glass.
Frame 1: base floating pose.
Frame 2: entire same body shifts UP one source pixel, hair tips another one pixel upwards, head/face keep exactly same contour.
Frame 3: remains at frame2 height, forearms raise one pixel, left foot extends down one pixel.
Frame 4: whole body returns to baseline height, hair tips drift one pixel towards right inside helmet, forearms remain slightly raised.
Frame 5: forearms return to base, right foot extends down one pixel, left foot returns.
Frame 6: baseline body, boots return to frame1, hair tips shift one pixel towards left to close the loop.
MOTIONS MUST BE EXTREMELY SUBTLE: this is calm suspended drifting with small balance adjustments, not running, jumping, swimming or waving. Use identical helmet/head/torso drawing translated, never redraw different anatomy. Tiny hand, boot and hair motion stagger across frames. Do not change helmet size or turn the head. Source pose and detailed source pixel style are the authority. Transparent sheet with roomy clear separation between six cells, complete boots and helmet in every frame.
animationExport: 96x112 RGBA cells; 16 opaque colours; fixed pose layers; idle 4x200ms; float 6x120ms; 8x nearest-neighbour transparent GIF previews.
